title: Classes & OOP
description: Access modifiers, abstract classes, implements, static members, and generic classes.

challenges.title: Access modifiers
challenges.whyMatters: Access modifiers appear in every OOP-style software engineering tool — loggers, HTTP clients, metric collectors. Knowing what's accessible where prevents subtle bugs when extending classes.
hints: private is only accessible in the class it's declared in; protected extends to subclasses

choices.label: private and protected are identical in TypeScript
private is class-only; protected is accessible in subclasses — so this.shared works in Child
protected is accessible everywhere; private is not
Both are runtime-enforced and throw if accessed incorrectly

challenges.title: readonly in classes
challenges.whyMatters: readonly on class properties is how you model immutable identifiers — service IDs, resource ARNs, connection strings that must not change after construction.
hints: readonly can be set in the constructor but nowhere else

choices.label: Works fine — readonly only prevents deletion
Compile error: cannot assign to 'id' because it is a read-only property
Runtime error only — TypeScript allows it but Node throws
Works because s is a const — readonly only applies to let variables

challenges.title: implements vs extends
challenges.whyMatters: implements is how you enforce a contract on a class without inheriting implementation — the AIProvider adapter pattern in this very repo uses it.
hints: extends inherits implementation; implements only enforces the shape at compile time

choices.label: They are identical — both inherit methods
extends inherits implementation from Base; implements only enforces that App satisfies the Logger shape
implements inherits implementation; extends only checks the shape
A class can only use one — you cannot combine extends and implements

challenges.title: Write a class with access modifiers
challenges.description:
Write a `ConnectionPool` class:

- `private readonly maxSize: number` — set in constructor
- `private connections: string[]` — starts empty
- `public add(conn: string): void` — adds if under maxSize, throws Error `'Pool is full'` if at capacity
- `public remove(conn: string): void` — removes if exists, throws Error `'Connection not found'` if missing
- `public get size(): number` — returns current count (getter)
- `public get available(): number` — returns maxSize - size
- `public list(): readonly string[]` — returns connections as readonly
challenges.whyMatters: Connection pools are fundamental software engineering infrastructure — database pools, HTTP client pools, gRPC channel pools all follow this exact pattern.
hints: readonly string[] prevents callers from mutating the internal array
throw new Error('Pool is full') in add when this.connections.length >= this.maxSize

challenges.title: Abstract classes
challenges.whyMatters: Abstract classes let you share implementation (like the run() method) while enforcing that subclasses provide the specific logic — perfect for a suite of health checkers with shared retry/logging behavior.
hints: Abstract classes can have concrete methods; interfaces cannot

choices.label: Abstract classes and interfaces are identical at runtime
Abstract classes can contain concrete implemented methods and cannot be instantiated directly — interfaces have no implementation
Abstract classes can be instantiated; interfaces cannot
Abstract classes compile to JavaScript classes; interfaces also compile to JavaScript interfaces

challenges.title: Abstract base class + implementations
challenges.description:
Write an abstract class `BaseHealthChecker`:
- `abstract readonly name: string`
- `abstract ping(): Promise<boolean>`
- `async check(): Promise<{ name: string; ok: boolean; latencyMs: number }>` — calls ping(), measures latency, catches errors (ok=false on throw)

Then write two concrete implementations:
- `HttpChecker(url: string)` — name is the url, ping() resolves true (simulate with `Promise.resolve(true)`)
- `TcpChecker(host: string, port: number)` — name is `host:port`, ping() resolves true
challenges.whyMatters: This is the exact pattern for building a suite of heterogeneous health checkers — each checker knows how to ping its own service, but the timing and error handling are shared.
hints: abstract readonly name: string — each subclass sets it as a class property
In check(), use Date.now() before and after ping()
Wrap ping() in try/catch — on Error, return ok: false

challenges.title: Generic class — typed repository
challenges.description:
Write a generic `Repository<T extends { id: string }>` class:

- `private store: Map<string, T>` — internal storage
- `save(entity: T): void` — stores by entity.id
- `findById(id: string): T | undefined`
- `findAll(): T[]`
- `delete(id: string): boolean` — returns true if existed
- `count(): number`

The class must work for any entity type that has an `id: string` field.
challenges.whyMatters: In-memory repositories are used for caching, test doubles, and config stores in production tooling. The generic constraint ensures type safety without knowing the entity shape in advance.
